questions.question: A boat can move at a speed of 5 km/h in still water. The sailor reaches a place by sailing at a speed of 6 km/h downstream and comes back in 1 hour. The place is at a distance of:
questions.questionHtml: A boat can move at a speed of 5 km/h in still water. The sailor reaches a place by sailing at a speed of 6 km/h downstream and comes back in 1 hour. The place is at a distance of:
questions.solution:
Downstream speed = still water speed + stream speed

Upstream speed = still water speed - stream speed

Boat's downstream speed = 5 + stream speed = 6 kmph

Boat's upstream speed = 5 - 1 = 4 kmph

Let the distance be x.

\(\dfrac{x}{6}\) + \(\dfrac{x}{4}\) = 1 ⇒ 5 km/hr \(\dfrac{2x + 3x}{12}\) = 1 ⇒ 5x = 12  ⇒ x = 2.4 km

questions.question: A motorboat goes 33 km upstream and 21 km downstream. The speed of the motorboat in still water is 25 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km h. Find the total time taken by the boat.
questions.questionHtml: A motorboat goes 33 km upstream and 21 km downstream. The speed of the motorboat in still water is 25 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km h. Find the total time taken by the boat.
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance upstream = 33 km

Distance downstream = 21 km

Speed of motorboat = 25 km/h

Speed of stream = 3 km/h

Concept used:

Let the Speed of the motorboat = v

And Speed of stream = u

Time taken by boat upstream and downstream = t

Distance covered by boat downstream = (v + u)t

Distance covered by boat upstream = (v - u)t

Calculation:

let the time taken be t

⇒ v - u = 25 - 3 = 22 km/h

⇒ v + u = 25 + 3 = 28 km/h

According to the question,

⇒ t = 33/(v - u) + 21/(v + u)

⇒ 33/22 + 21/28

⇒ 3/2 + 3/4

⇒ 2.25 h

After converting 0.25 h in minutes,

⇒ t = 2 h 15 min

∴Total time taken by boat is 2 h 15 min.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 6 kmph and the speed of the stream is 1.5 kmph . A man rows to a place at a distance of 22.5 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a boat in still water is 6 kmph and the speed of the stream is 1.5 kmph. A man rows to a place at a distance of 22.5 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:
questions.solution:
Upstream speed of the boat = 6 – 1.5 = 4.5 kmph

Downstream speed of the boat = 6 + 1.5 = 7.5 kmph

Total time taken by the man = \(\frac{22.5}{4.5}\) + \(\frac{22.5}{7.5}\) = 5 + 3 = 8 hours

questions.question: A boat can go 10 km upstream and 11 km downstream in a total time of 52 minutes, If the speed of the stream is 5 km/h, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat when going downstream?
questions.questionHtml: A boat can go 10 km upstream and 11 km downstream in a total time of 52 minutes, If the speed of the stream is 5 km/h, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat when going downstream?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total time taken by boat = 52 minutes

Distance travelled upstream = 10 km

Distance traveled downstream = 11 km

Speed of the stream = 5 km/h

Concept used:

Time = Distance/speed

Upstream speed = u - v

Downstream speed = u + v

(a2 - b2) = (a + b)(a - b)

Here, u = speed of the object

v = speed of the stream

Calculation:

Let the speed of the boat be x km/h

According to the question,

\(\frac{10}{x-5}+\frac{11}{x+5}=\frac{52}{60}\)

⇒ \(\frac{10}{x-5}+\frac{11}{x+5}=\frac{13}{15}\)

⇒ \(\frac{10x+50+11x-55}{(x-5)(x+5)}=\frac{13}{15}\)

⇒ \(\frac{21x-5}{(x^2-25)}=\frac{13}{15}\)

⇒ 315x - 75 = 13x2 - 325

⇒ 13x2 - 325 + 75 - 315x = 0

⇒ 13x2 - 315x - 250 = 0

⇒ 13x2 - 325x + 10x - 250 = 0

⇒ 13x(x - 25) + 10(x - 25) = 0

⇒ (x - 25)(13x + 10) = 0

So, x = 25 or - (10/13)

As speed cannot be negative so x = 25

Speed of the boat = 25 km/h

So, downstream speed = 25 + 5 = 30 km/h

∴ The speed (in km/h) of the boat when going downstream is 30.

Shortcut Trick

Time taken to go upstream = 10/(u - v)

Time taken to go downstream = 11/(u + v)

⇒ 10/(u - v) + 11/(u + v) = 52/60

⇒ 10/(u - 5) + 11/(u + 5) = 52/60

Put the value of "u" from the option i.e.

Put u = 25 and equate the values

⇒ 10/20 + 11/30 = 52/60

⇒ (30 + 22)/60 = 52/60

⇒ 52/60 = 52/60

Hence the speed of the boat is 25 km/hr

Downstream speed = 25 + 5 = 30 km/hr

Mistake PointsDownstream speed⇒ speed of the boat+speed of water

Upstream Speed ⇒ speed of the boat- speed of water

questions.question: A boat covers a distance of 2 km upstream and 4 km downstream in 120 minutes. It covers a distance of 4 km upstream and 6 km downstream in 210 minutes. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.questionHtml: A boat covers a distance of 2 km upstream and 4 km downstream in 120 minutes. It covers a distance of 4 km upstream and 6 km downstream in 210 minutes. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:

questions.question: A boat takes 20 hours to travel downstream from point P to point Q and to come back to a point R which is at midway between P and Q. If the velocity of the stream is 6 km/h and the speed of the boat in still water is 18 km/h, what is the distance between P and Q?
questions.questionHtml: A boat takes 20 hours to travel downstream from point P to point Q and to come back to a point R which is at midway between P and Q. If the velocity of the stream is 6 km/h and the speed of the boat in still water is 18 km/h, what is the distance between P and Q?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of boat in still water (x) = 18 km/h

Speed of current(y) = 6 km/h

Total time = 20 h

Let the distance between points P and Q = 2Z

R is the midpoint between P & Q

RP = RQ = \(\frac {PQ}{2}\)= Z

Formula used:

Total Time = Total Distance/Speed

Downstream (D)= ( x + y ) = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h

Upstream(U)= ( x - y ) = 18 - 6 = 12 km/h

Calculation:

\(T = \frac {2Z}{D} + \frac {Z}{U}\)

\(20 = \frac {2Z}{24} + \frac {Z}{12}\)

Z = 120 km 

∴ the distance between P and Q (2Z) = 2 × 120 = 240 km.

The answer is 240 km.

questions.question: The speed of a stream is 9 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 56 km downstream and 28 km upstream in 7 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">The speed of a stream is 9 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 56 km downstream and 28 km upstream in 7 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).</font></font>
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time = Ddown / (B + S) + Dup / (B − S)

⇒ 7 = 56 / (B + 9) + 28 / (B − 9)

⇒ 1 = 8 / (B + 9) + 4 / (B − 9) (Dividing by 7 on both sides)

Checking the options, for B = 15 km/h: 8 / 24 + 4 / 6 = 1/3 + 2/3 = 1 (Equation satisfied)

∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of stream (S) = 9 km/h

Distance downstream (Dd) = 56 km

Distance upstream (Du) = 28 km

Total time (T) = 7 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = Dd / (B + S) + Du / (B − S)

Calculations:

⇒ 56 / (B + 9) + 28 / (B − 9) = 7

⇒ 8 / (B + 9) + 4 / (B − 9) = 1

⇒ [8(B − 9) + 4(B + 9)] / [(B + 9)(B − 9)] = 1

⇒ 8B − 72 + 4B + 36 = B2 − 81

⇒ 12B − 36 = B2 − 81

⇒ B2 − 12B − 45 = 0

⇒ B2 − 15B + 3B − 45 = 0

⇒ B(B − 15) + 3(B − 15) = 0

⇒ (B − 15)(B + 3) = 0

⇒ B = 15 or B = −3

⇒ Since speed cannot be negative, B = 15 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.

Additional Information

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

If the speed of a boat in still water is B and the speed of the stream is S, then downstream speed = B + S and upstream speed = B − S.

Finding Speed from Downstream & Upstream

Speed of boat in still water (B) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream (S) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed

When a boat travels equal distances downstream and upstream, its average speed for the entire journey is given by (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Speed of boat in still water.

questions.question: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.questionHtml: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.solution:
Speed upstream = 54 km / 6 h = 9 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = 9 km/h + 4.8 km/h = 13.8 km/h

Speed downstream = 13.8 km/h + 4.8 km/h = 18.6 km/h

Time = 279 km / 18.6 km/h = 15 hours

questions.question: A motorboat, travelling at the same speed, can cover 25 km upstream and 39 km downstream in 8 hrs. At the same speed, it can travel 35 km upstream and 52 km downstream in 11 hrs. The speed of the stream is:
questions.questionHtml: A motorboat, travelling at the same speed, can cover 25 km upstream and 39 km downstream in 8 hrs. At the same speed, it can travel 35 km upstream and 52 km downstream in 11 hrs. The speed of the stream is:
questions.solution:
Mathematically, it can be written as:

\(\Rightarrow \frac{25}{u-v} + \frac{39}{u+v} = 8 \)     ----(1)

The time is taken by the motorboat to cover 25 km upstream and 39 km downstream = 11 hours

\(\Rightarrow \frac{35}{u-v} + \frac{52}{u+v} = 11\)     ----(2)

Divide the equation (1) by 3 and equation (2) by 4 and then subtract equation (2) from (1),

\(\Rightarrow \frac{100}{u-v}-\frac{105}{u-v} = 1 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{5}{u-v} = 1\)

\(\Rightarrow {u-v} = 5\)     ----(3)

Substitute the equation (3) in equation (1).

\(\Rightarrow \frac{25}{5} + \frac{39}{u+v} = 8 \\ \Rightarrow 5 + \frac{39}{u+v} = 8 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{39}{u+v} = 3 \)h

\(\Rightarrow u+v=13 \)     ----(4)

Now, subtract equation (3) from (4) we get,

\(\Rightarrow 2v = 8 \\ \Rightarrow v = 4\)

∴ The speed of stream is 4 kmph.

questions.question: The speed of a steamer in still water is 8 km/h, while the river is flowing with a speed of 4 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 2h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a steamer in still water is 8 km/h, while the river is flowing with a speed of 4 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 2h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.solution:
Given:

The speed of a steamer in still water is 8 km/h

the river is flowing at a speed of 4 km/h.

The time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 2h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream.

Concept used:

Distance = speed × time

Calculation:

Let the distance be d km

As per the question,

d / (8 - 4)   - d / (8 + 4) = 2 

⇒ d / 4 - d / 12 = 2

⇒ 2d / 12 = 2

⇒ d = 12 km

The distance is 12 km
